categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Developer Activity

content.text: On July 17, 2026, the ElizaOS community discussion channel saw a handful of brief interactions. A community call for a project called Zeroclaw was announced and taking place, with at least one member asking to join. One user expressed skepticism about the future of ElizaOS, stating that not even Justin Sun could save it. A developer posted asking if anyone was looking to hire a developer. Activity in the coders channel was minimal, consisting of a single emoji reply between two members.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Token Sentiment

content.text: In the ElizaOS Discord discussion channel, a brief conversation took place on July 18, 2026 regarding the future of the ElizaOS token. One user expressed a bearish outlook, claiming that exchanges would delist the token within two months followed by a significant price decline. Another user pushed back on this sentiment, acknowledging that while the tokenomics may not look ideal, elizaOS is actively building and developing meaningful products. A third user reacted to the exchange with amusement. The coders channel had no activity recorded for the same date.

categories.title: Scam Activity and Security Warnings in Community Channels

content.text: On July 19, 2026, a user identified as MR james posted identical messages across both the general discussion channel and the coders channel, claiming to have made $31,000 from rugging meme coins and offering to teach others how to conduct rug pulls. The user solicited direct messages from interested parties, framing the offer as free help. This activity was flagged as a scam. In the discussion channel, a community helper known as THE UNDERRATED MAJ warned another user, El_Lince, not to click any scam support links, not to accept direct messages from unknown users, and to report anyone who sends unsolicited DMs. The warnings received positive reactions from community members. Separately, El_Lince had asked why the updates channel was not working, which appeared to be unrelated to the scam activity. The channel topic for the coders channel directs users to the official ElizaOS documentation at docs.elizaos.ai for getting started with agent development.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Activity and Project Status

content.text: Community members in the discussion channel expressed concern about the apparent inactivity of the ElizaOS project and its Discord server. One member noted that the only visible signs of life from the community are GitHub updates, and suggested monitoring the elizaos-github Discord channel for activity. Speculation arose that the silence may be related to ongoing legal proceedings or a deliberate decision to stay quiet until an anticipated app release. Members also noted that communication has been declining despite previous promises, and even spam activity in the channel has ceased. A developer posted asking if anyone was looking to hire, suggesting some community members remain engaged despite the low activity.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: AI Agents, Market Outlook, and Builder Activity

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members raised questions about multiplayer AI agents and whether such a concept is feasible. Market sentiment was also discussed, with one member noting that big investors are expected to return from vacations in Autumn, which could influence market conditions. Another member commented that market makers tend to wait for holders to sell before pumping prices, expressing confidence that Eliza will not simply disappear. Additionally, it was mentioned that the ai16z DAO, potentially rebranded as Eliza DAO, could operate on the Robinhood chain.

In the coders channel, several AI engineers introduced themselves and expressed interest in collaborating on projects involving AI agents, agentic workflows, LLM integrations, multi-agent systems, RAG, MCP, full-stack development, robotics, and game development. One member announced the release of a new skill called Neverbell, which gives AI agents market access, and invited community feedback. Another member shared Cipher Vault, a browser-based GameFi demo running on Solana Devnet that uses an Eliza AI Oracle agent to generate daily riddles. The game involves harvesting in-game currency, paying tributes, and solving puzzles, with all activity settled as on-chain SPL token transfers on Devnet. A community member also encouraged builders to create a trading agent on the Robinhood chain to take advantage of the current bull market.

categories.title: Community Sentiment on DEGENAI and ElizaOS Future

content.text: Discussion in the community channel reflects a largely pessimistic outlook on the future of DEGENAI and ElizaOS. One user noted that AI trading is considered a major trend for the next bull market and expressed hope that DEGENAI could perform well, with ElizaOS potentially benefiting as a result. However, other community members pushed back, suggesting the projects are effectively dead and that most participants have moved on. A point of concern raised was that even shaw, a key figure associated with ElizaOS, no longer posts anything related to the project on his social media. One user cautioned that launching new coins to replace abandoned ones would be counterproductive, as it would erode trust. The overall tone of the conversation suggests the community has lost confidence in the current trajectory of both projects, with faint hope that something new might emerge in the next bull market cycle.

categories.title: Crypto Market Conditions: Bear vs Bull Debate and Alt Season Discussion

content.text: On July 23, 2026, users in the discussion channel debated whether the crypto market is currently in a bear or bull market. One user argued it remains a bear market until the top 100 coins by market cap each reach at least 1 billion dollars in market capitalization, referencing conditions seen in late 2020 and mid 2025 as benchmarks for a true bull market. Another user countered that major cap coins like Ethereum are in a bear market and that everything else is just noise. A third user pushed back on both, stating that crypto is no longer a small market where everything moves together, and that it now moves in sectors. This user pointed to onchain markets, specifically the Robinhood chain, as currently experiencing a bull market, while majors lag behind. The conversation also touched on Ethereum not having had a meaningful bull run in over five years, only recently breaking above its 2021 high in August 2025. Users attributed this partly to a poor macro environment and tightening monetary policy over the past five years. The discussion also noted that past narratives such as AI coins, meme coins following the 2024 presidential election, RWA, and the Robinhood chain have each drawn attention in cycles, similar to how attention drove the semiconductor stock market. One user expressed doubt that a broad alt season like 2021 would return, while another insisted alt season is already happening in specific sectors and that participants are missing the point by focusing only on majors. The conversation briefly extended to rising memory and smartphone prices as a reflection of broader macro pressures, with one user humorously suggesting that cheap memory prices might signal the return of a broad alt season.
